clue.text: No night-light eclipses very old one used underground

indicators.note: to eclipse is to cover over, so the first pair of words surround the abbreviation for very

parts.note: where there is no night there is day
a lamp gives light

explanation.surface: A night-light outshines an elderly miner's torch down the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eclipses' covers V. The Davy lamp was the flame safety lamp for coal miners invented by Humphry Davy in 1815.
explanation.definitionFit: The Davy lamp was the historic flame safety lamp carried by coal miners in the pits.

clue.text: Rug cosy, but not right for native American home

parts.note: rug is slang for a wig

indicators.note: the second word's synonym must lose its letter for right

parts.note: cosy means warm
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A snug blanket for a tepee-style home, minus something on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A wigwam is a domed dwelling of some North American indigenous peoples.

clue.text: Slow, rather like pellets?

definitions.meaning: slugs are bullets or pellets, so slug-ish is whimsically like them

explanation.definitionFit: Sluggish is a standard synonym for slow, lacking speed and energy.

clue.text: In American literature, stop for some time

definitions.meaning: Americans call the full stop at the end of a sentence a ...

explanation.surface: In American books, pause for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: US usage names the full stop punctuation mark this way; it also means an era or span.

clue.text: Lose head in temper on frequent occasions

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the synonym goes

parts.note: to temper is to soften, moderate
the initial letter dropped

explanation.surface: Someone frequently loses their head in a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temper' is a verb here (soften), not anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means many times, repeatedly, frequently.

clue.text: Peer into precise feature on a car

indicators.note: one word goes inside the other here, the noble entering the synonym for precise

parts.note: right as in correct, exact
an earl is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: Someone peers at a precise detail on a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear light is the red lamp fitted at the back of a vehicle.

clue.text: Lofty publication has nothing new in quote that's ludicrous

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a publication
nil means nothing

indicators.note: the letter for new goes inside the word quote
a ludicrous version of the letters is a jumbled one

explanation.surface: A highbrow magazine prints a ridiculous new quotation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's ludicrous' rearranges QUNOTE (N inside QUOTE) to OQUENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Magniloquent means grandiose or pompous in speech, a lofty style.

clue.text: One putting up a German cowboy?

parts.note: Jerry is old British slang for a German
a builder puts up buildings

explanation.surface: A German who builds is likened to a cowboy.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a cowboy is a dishonest, shoddy tradesman, which is just what a jerry-builder is.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerry-builder erects cheap, badly made houses: a cowboy in UK trade slang.

clue.text: Flower behind river in darkish purple, on recollection

parts.note: the behind is the butt, the bottom

indicators.note: the river's letter goes inside the colour word once turned round
recollection read as re-collection, calling back, so the colour runs backwards

parts.note: puce is a brownish purple

explanation.surface: A flower is remembered behind a river, in a dark purple shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on recollection' turns PUCE into ECUP; R goes in after its E.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common yellow wild flower of the genus Ranunculus.

clue.text: I dressed in blue for the most part, ending in pale green

indicators.note: the letter I is clothed by the colour
most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: navy is a dark blue
the last letter dropped

indicators.note: only the last letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: I am dressed largely in blue with a touch of pale green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' is not a colour here: it means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in the sense of inexperienced or innocent is a synonym for naive.

clue.text: As one understands initially and informally, darkness heading for dawn

indicators.note: only the first letter of the preceding word is taken

parts.note: nite is an informal spelling of night, darkness

indicators.note: the front letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone grasps at once that the darkness will soon give way to dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting as one means acting together, united in purpose.

clue.text: Relaxing novel deviates

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: A relaxing book that strays from the norm.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative drug is calming, relaxing the patient.

clue.text: Swallow, one settling finally into its home?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the single letter is placed inside the home word

parts.note: a bird's home is its nest

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word before

explanation.surface: A swallow settles at last into its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird reading of 'Swallow' paints the scene; the definition is the verb, to take in food.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food into the body by swallowing.

clue.text: Second year held by continental of an ancient empire

indicators.note: the second and third pieces are gripped inside the first

parts.note: an Asian is a native of the continent of Asia

explanation.surface: A second year spent with someone from a continent of an old empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Assyria was an ancient Mesopotamian empire, so the adjective describes things belonging to it.

clue.text: Oppressor free of blemish?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as ..., to remove a spot

explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who wields power cruelly, an oppressor.

clue.text: Chambers takes a running jump?

definitions.meaning: a gymnast or athlete ... after a run-up

explanation.surface: Rooms leap into action.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaults are arched chambers, such as cellars or burial crypts, beneath buildings.

clue.text: Fabulous line ready to broadcast, filled with information

indicators.note: the scrambled word has the information word put inside it
broadcast as scattered, so the letters are spread out anew

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A great line ready to go on air, packed with facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means of fable here, not marvellous; 'to broadcast' scatters the letters of ready to EDARY before the filling goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabulous in its old sense means belonging to fable or legend.

clue.text: Wrongly say menu needs scorpion in a stew

indicators.note: being in a stew is being in a muddle, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A menu that demands scorpion stew.
explanation.definitionFit: To mispronounce a word is to say it wrongly.

clue.text: I signed contract that's just right

parts.note: a deal is a signed agreement

explanation.surface: I put my name to a contract that suits perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means perfect, exactly as it should be.

clue.text: Worm, perhaps, runs into another worm?

indicators.note: the cricket letter for runs goes inside the other creature

parts.note: a wiggler is a fishing worm or wriggling larva
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: One worm crawls into another.
explanation.definitionFit: A wriggler is anything that squirms, a worm being a classic example.

clue.text: Contemplate change in partner

indicators.note: the synonym for change goes inside the partner word

parts.note: a mate is a partner
to edit is to change text

explanation.surface: Think about changing your spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to think deeply, to ponder or reflect.

clue.text: Secure boats, cutters

parts.note: to nail is to fasten securely
clippers are fast sailing ships

explanation.surface: Fasten the boats and the cutters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutters' looks like more boats, but here it is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Nail clippers are a small cutting tool for trimming fingernails.

clue.text: Monarch, name possibly in doubt

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the doubt word

parts.note: a query is a doubt or question

indicators.note: possibly hints that the word may take another form, a jumble

explanation.surface: A monarch's name may be in question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' jumbles the name to ENMA. 'Monarch' fits as a reigning queen; the liner of that name is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary I and Mary II were reigning English queens, each a monarch in her own right.

clue.text: Sail off amid endless noise, land on the Horn of Africa

definitions.text: land on the Horn of Africa

indicators.note: the sail and off words sit in the middle of the noise word
the noise word loses its final letter

parts.note: din is a loud noise
the final letter dropped
a jib is a triangular sail
off as in out, away

explanation.surface: A sail gets away amid constant din, landing on the African coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Djibouti is a small country on the Horn of Africa by the Gulf of Aden.

clue.text: Fine to poke amphibian that's producing foam

indicators.note: the fine word is poked into the amphibian

parts.note: a frog is an amphibian
fine as in thin, slender

explanation.surface: A thin stick pokes a frog until it foams.
explanation.definitionFit: Frothing means bubbling or foaming.

clue.text: Irish turned up north of little Italian port

indicators.note: in a down entry, north of puts the first piece above the next
in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: mini means little

explanation.surface: An Irishman shows up north of a small Italian harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a seaside port on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Long-distance runner cut over peak in Nepal

indicators.note: in a down entry, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: to sever is to cut

indicators.note: the peak of a word is its top or first letter

explanation.surface: A marathon man is cut down on a Himalayan peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is a river: the SEVERN is Britain's longest.
explanation.definitionFit: A river runs, and the Severn is the longest river in Britain.

clue.text: Chance to join hands at bridge with girl

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
North and South are two of the four hands, or players, at bridge

explanation.surface: A chance to join a girl at the bridge table.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens means an even chance in betting, odds of one to one.
